metadata.note: The Philadelphia, Wilmington and Baltimore Rail Road (1838-1902): the Philadelphia - Wilmington - Baltimore main line, drawn in era pieces so that each era sits on its own alignment (Rule 2) - the original Gray's Ferry route and the Broad & Washington approach, the 1872 Darby route, the Susquehanna ferry gap (no rail drawn 1838-1866) and the 1866 bridge, and the two Baltimore approaches (President Street to 1873, Union Tunnel from 1873) - plus the New Castle and Frenchtown (1843-1855), the Delaware Division (Delaware Railroad, leased from 1857), Newark - Delaware City, the Smyrna, Oxford, Townsend - Centreville and Seaford - Cambridge branches, the Columbia and Port Deposit (from 1884) and the West Chester line (from 1880). One feature per drawable span and alignment, all one company and one colour (#1F6F78, new to data/). 1881: the PRR bought a stock majority; that is NOT treated as a split, matching the Wilmington and Northern precedent where a stock purchase without a lease kept the original operator - the PW&B stayed the operating company (leasing the B&P to itself in 1891, issuing its own annual reports) until the 1 Nov 1902 merger into the Philadelphia, Baltimore and Washington. This PR adds this one layer only: overlaps with existing features are recorded in existing_layer_overlap, not edited.
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), traced with opstrace.py. Probed old_railway_operator, historic:operator and note:old_railway_operator across PA/DE/MD: no way carries a PW&B spelling in old_railway_operator - ex-PW&B lines are tagged old_railway_operator=PRR with note:old_railway_operator 'PB&W', 'PB&W (Delaware)' or 'leased from PRR (PB&W)' (the old Gray's Ferry line, later Reading), and the Northeast Corridor carries historic:operator 'Philadelphia, Baltimore and Washington Railroad'. Lines were separated by name and corridor with waypoints (research/notes/osm-delmarva-prr-eastern-shore.md); railway=abandoned/razed/demolished ways were fetched separately (research/notes/opstrace-drops-railway-demolished.md).

OpenHistoricalMap (CC0): unusually complete dated PW&B ways (cited there to Coverdale & Colpitts) - the 1838 Gray's Ferry route and Washington Avenue approach, the 1872 Darby route, the 1837 Claymont and Elkton lines, the 1837-1866 ferry spurs and 1866-1906 bridge line at the Susquehanna, the New Castle and Frenchtown, the Oxford, Townsend and Cambridge branches, and the 1877-1928 C&PD line at Conowingo. Geometry only: no OHM date is used as a source for any segment (research/notes/openhistoricalmap-geometry-source.md). An era-aware cost penalised OHM ways built after a feature's start year, so later alignments were not picked where an era one exists.
Baltimore street geometry (Boston Street, Fleet Street) from OSM highway centrelines for the President Street approach.

Waypoints: Nominatim, each type checked; county answers for 'Chester, PA', 'New Castle, DE' and 'Columbia, PA', a school for 'Delmar, DE' and the wrong (Susquehanna) Frenchtown were replaced by hand-placed points on the line.
existing_layer_overlap: pennsylvania_railroad.geojson prr-mainline-new-york-washington ('Pennsylvania Railroad: New York - Washington (Northeast Corridor)', #7B241C) draws the Philadelphia - Baltimore corridor from 1838 under the PRR's name, on the modern alignment for every era (30th Street, Darby, the 1906 Susquehanna bridge, the Union Tunnel) - it duplicates every main-line feature here 1838-1902. The report lists this as a Rule 4 and Rule 2 defect; fixing it (cutting the PRR feature's 1838-1902 Philadelphia - Baltimore years) is left for a follow-up PR.

not_yet_sourced: All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates; the only timed service found is the 1839 daily mail train (about 6.5 h end to end).

1881-1902 display: PW&B or PRR? No 1880s-90s Official Guide heading or newspaper timetable was checked to see whether these trains were advertised as Pennsylvania Railroad trains (report UNRESOLVED 1).

Philadelphia terminal after 1866: when regular PW&B trains left Broad & Washington (Fowler 4A also gives Philadelphia (1st) as 1839>1852, and the station was used for 1876 Centennial and 1918 specials). The approach to West Philadelphia (1866-1881) and the PRR's Broad Street Station (from Dec 1881) is not drawn in PW&B colour, so the Darby route and the 1866-1872 Gray's Ferry route stop at Gray's Ferry.
President Street after 1873: Fowler says the route served until 1873, Wikipedia says some passenger trains until 1911 - not reconciled.
New Castle and Frenchtown: end bracket 1855-1857 (abandonment dated 1857 and 1859 by different sources); operator 1839-1843 unknown.
Operators of the subsidiaries: the P&BC (and so the West Chester line from 1881), the QA&K 1871-1877; the Oxford line ('1871 or earlier') and Cambridge ('as agent' 1883) are second-hand.
Columbia and Port Deposit: passenger start bracket 1877-1884 (drawn from Fowler's 1884 letter); whether the Holtwood or Safe Harbor dams relocated any of the line.
Smyrna Branch: the 1866 opening is uncited and the Smyrna (2nd) station site is not pinned.
Newark - Delaware City drawn 11.8 mi against Fowler's 12.3 mi.

properties.line: Philadelphia, Wilmington and Baltimore: Broad & Washington – Gray's Ferry
properties.speed_source: estimated, not sourced (Rule 3). The only timed PW&B service found is an 1839 advertisement: Baltimore 9:30 a.m. to Philadelphia (Market St) 4 p.m., about 6.5 h for roughly 100 mi including the Susquehanna ferry and the horse-drawn street legs (Wikipedia PW&B article).
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror) and OpenHistoricalMap (CC0), traced with opstrace.py; OHM used for geometry only, its dates are never a source.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced, no straight-line leg: 2.29 mi drawn against about 2-3 mi documented (Fowler SL 217 table 4A mileposts 0/1/2/2/3). Follows OpenHistoricalMap's dated PW&B ways along Washington Avenue and over the Gray's Ferry (Newkirk Viaduct) crossing of the Schuylkill; OSM still has abandoned PW&B-noted ways named 'Washington Avenue' on the same line. Ends at the west bank, where it meets the original Gray's Ferry route.

segments.note: Philadelphia terminal approach of the PW&B: Broad & Washington (Prime) Streets - South Street - Gray's Ferry. Drawn from 1839, the first year both sources agree the terminal was in use: the Gray's Ferry bridge opened Dec 1838 (Wikipedia PW&B) and Fowler 4A lists 'Philadelphia (1st) (1839>1852)' at Broad & Washington. Drawn to 1866, when main-line trains began using West Philadelphia (PWB) (1866>1881, Fowler table 4). Whether some regular trains stayed at Broad & Washington after 1866 is NOT established (the station was rebuilt for the 1876 Centennial and used for specials); the end is the last confirmed year, not a known end. Rule 5: from 1842 to 1852 the cars went on beyond Broad & Washington by HORSE along Broad and Market Streets to 11th & Market (Fowler 4A); that street haulage is not drawn. Headway is an estimate, not counted from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: 1839 start from Fowler SL 217 table 4A ('Philadelphia (1st) (1839>1852)') and the Dec 1838 bridge date in Wikipedia; 1866 end from Fowler table 4 ('West Philadelphia (PWB) (1866>1881)'), a last-confirmed year. Headway not sourced.

Gray's Ferry - Lester follows OpenHistoricalMap ways dated 1838 (Coverdale & Colpitts); Eastwick - Lester also matches the OSM ways noted 'leased from PRR (PB&W)' (later the Reading's Philadelphia & Chester Branch, today the SEPTA Airport Line and Chester Secondary); Lester - Eddystone follows the razed/abandoned OSM ways of the same branch. The last 70 m is a tie to the main line at Eddystone.

segments.note: The PW&B's original main line, Gray's Ferry - Eastwick (Tinicum marshes) - Eddystone, part of the line opened Wilmington - Gray's Ferry on 15 Jan 1838 (Wikipedia PW&B). Replaced for passenger trains by the inland Darby Improvement, opened 18 Nov 1872; the old line was leased to the Reading from 1 Jul 1873 'with the stipulation that it would be used solely for freight' - those freight years are not drawn (Rule 1). The B&O ran its Washington - Philadelphia trains over the PW&B on trackage rights from 1838. In 1838 itself trains terminated at Gray's Ferry until the Schuylkill bridge opened in December. Headway is an estimate, not counted from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: 1838 opening (15 Jan 1838) and the 18 Nov 1872 Darby Improvement from Wikipedia PW&B; Fowler SL 217 tables 4/4A ('PRR main line originally via [later Reading RR] between Arsenal Junction and Chester'). Headway not sourced.

properties.line: Philadelphia, Wilmington and Baltimore: Main Line (Darby route)
properties.speed_source: estimated, not sourced (Rule 3). The only timed PW&B service found is an 1839 advertisement: Baltimore 9:30 a.m. to Philadelphia (Market St) 4 p.m., about 6.5 h for roughly 100 mi including the Susquehanna ferry and the horse-drawn street legs (Wikipedia PW&B article).

properties.geometry_quality: Traced, no straight-line leg: 9.75 mi drawn (Arsenal / Gray's Ferry west bank - Darby - Glenolden - Ridley Park - Eddystone). The report gives no separate mileage for this stretch; it compares with 9.9 mi for the old line it replaced. Follows OpenHistoricalMap ways dated 18 Nov 1872, which lie within 8 m of today's Northeast Corridor. The north end stops at the Gray's Ferry junction: trains ran on to West Philadelphia (1866-1881) and the PRR's Broad Street Station (from Dec 1881) over track this layer does not draw in PW&B colour (see not_yet_sourced).

segments.note: The Darby Improvement inland line, opened 18 Nov 1872 (Wikipedia PW&B), which took the PW&B's trains off the original Gray's Ferry - Eastwick route. The PRR ran its through New York - Washington trains over the PW&B from 1873 under a through-running agreement; the B&O's trackage rights ran until 12 Oct 1884. The PRR bought a majority of PW&B stock in 1881; that is a stock purchase, not a lease, and the PW&B stayed the operating company (it leased the B&P to itself in 1891 and kept issuing its own annual reports), so 1881 is not a split here. 1902 is the end of this company: the PW&B merged with the Baltimore and Potomac into the Philadelphia, Baltimore and Washington on 1 Nov 1902; the line carried on under the PB&W (see the Pennsylvania Railroad layer). Headway is an estimate, not counted from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: 1872 opening from Wikipedia PW&B (Darby Improvement, 18 Nov 1872); 1902 end is the PB&W merger (Wikipedia PW&B). B&O end date from the CSX Susquehanna River Bridge article (read through a search summary). Headway not sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced, no straight-line leg: 47.19 mi drawn Eddystone - Perryville (1st) ferry wharf; the Wilmington - Perryville part measures 32.9 mi against 32.2 mi documented (Fowler SL 216 table 1: Wilmington 26.7, Perryville 58.9). Drawn on the ORIGINAL alignment wherever OpenHistoricalMap or OSM keeps it: the old line through Claymont (OHM ways dated 1838 and the OSM 'Claymont Industrial Track'), the Iron Hill - Elkton (1st) - Bacon Hill old line (OHM 1837-1934 ways and abandoned OSM PB&W ways), the curve west of Elkton that OHM dates 1837-1898 (spliced in from OHM), and the pre-1906 approach to Perryville (OHM 1837-1906) ending at the 1837-1866 ferry spur. LATER-ALIGNMENT CAVEATS: (1) the original line is drawn for every year to 1902, so the Claymont / Naaman's Creek straightening (1895 per Wikipedia, 'until 1902' per Fowler note 1 - a conflict) and the 1898 curve change west of Elkton are not shown for their last few PW&B years; (2) elsewhere (Chester - Wilmington - Newark, North East - Charlestown) the drawn track is today's Northeast Corridor, and no other realignment in those stretches is recorded in the report, but none was checked either. The Elkton old line is right for the whole PW&B era (the 1935 cut-off is not drawn).

segments.note: Wilmington - Perryville was built by the Wilmington and Susquehanna (track by July 1837, with ferry-connected trains); Wilmington - Gray's Ferry opened 15 Jan 1838 and the three companies merged as the PW&B on 12 Feb 1838 (Wikipedia PW&B). The 1837 predecessor months are not drawn (see metadata). Perryville (1st) was the ferry landing: the Susquehanna was crossed by steam ferry - the 'Susquehanna', from 1853 the car ferry 'Maryland' - until the bridge opened in Nov 1866; that crossing is not drawn as rail. B&O through trains used the line on trackage rights from 1838. Headway is an estimate, not counted from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: 1837 track, 15 Jan 1838 opening and 12 Feb 1838 merger from Wikipedia PW&B; ferry boats from the Havre de Grace history listing (read through a search summary). Headway not sourced.

Winter 1852: tracks were laid on the ice from 15 Jan to 24 Feb (some accounts 29 Feb) and passengers crossed by horse-drawn sled - animal power, not drawn (Rule 5). The 1866 bridge was superseded by the 1906 bridge in the PB&W era. The PRR bought a majority of PW&B stock in 1881; that is a stock purchase, not a lease, and the PW&B stayed the operating company (it leased the B&P to itself in 1891 and kept issuing its own annual reports), so 1881 is not a split here. 1902 is the end of this company: the PW&B merged with the Baltimore and Potomac into the Philadelphia, Baltimore and Washington on 1 Nov 1902; the line carried on under the PB&W (see the Pennsylvania Railroad layer). Bay View - Canton follows the active OSM 'President Street Track' (Norfolk Southern / Canton Railroad); Canton - President Street follows the OSM centrelines of Boston Street and Fleet Street, the streets the report names for the line (via Canton, Clinton Street, Broadway), so the exact track position beside or in those streets is APPROXIMATED to the street grid (about 2 mi). segments.note: The original PW&B (ex Baltimore and Port Deposit) approach: Bay View - Canton - Boston and Fleet Streets - President Street. President Street station opened 18 Feb 1850; before that the terminus was a few hundred yards away at President & Fleet (Wikipedia President Street Station). Fowler 1A: the 'original PWB ... route to Baltimore until opening of line to Calvert Station 1873'. CONFLICT: Wikipedia says the station 'served some passenger trains until 1911'; local trains after 1873 are not confirmed for the PW&B era and are not drawn. Rule 5: through cars for Washington were drawn by HORSES along Pratt Street to the B&O station (the city banned locomotives there); that street haulage is not drawn. Headway is an estimate, not counted from a timetable.

properties.line: Philadelphia, Wilmington and Baltimore: New Castle – Frenchtown
properties.speed_source: estimated, not sourced (Rule 3): no running time for this line was found in any source.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror) and OpenHistoricalMap (CC0), traced with opstrace.py; OHM used for geometry only, its dates are never a source.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced on OpenHistoricalMap, no straight-line leg: 16.46 mi drawn against about 16 mi documented (commonly given; Wikipedia). Follows OHM's New Castle and Frenchtown ways (dated 1832, the west part ending 1859) from the Elk River landing at Frenchtown to the New Castle wharf; it passes through the OSM abandoned ways named 'New Castle and Frenchtown Railway' near Bear. Almost all of it is lifted; the east end into New Castle is the line later kept as part of the Delaware Branch.

segments.note: The New Castle and Frenchtown: Delaware's first steam railroad and the original boat-rail-boat Philadelphia - Baltimore route. The PW&B bought control on 15 Mar 1839 and, per Wikipedia, 'in 1843 the NC&F was completely absorbed by the PW&B' - the earliest date a source treats the PW&B as owner-operator, so it is drawn from 1843 (who ran the trains 1839-1843 is not established; formal merger 1877). Ends 1855, the year the connecting steamboats stopped: the end is bracketed 1855-1857 (Fowler '1832 > 1856'; Cecil County part abandoned March 1857 per Wikipedia NC&F; 1859 west of Bear per Wikipedia PW&B) and is drawn at the earliest. Rule 5: the NC&F used horses for about a year after opening in 1832 - outside this span anyway. Headway is an estimate, not counted from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: 1843 absorption and 1855 end of the boats from Wikipedia NC&F; Fowler SL 216 table 59 ('1832 > 1856'); abandonment conflict from Wikipedia PW&B and Delaware Railroad. Headway not sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced, no straight-line leg: 84.25 mi drawn Wilmington - New Castle - Bear (Porter jct) - Middletown - Clayton - Dover - Harrington - Seaford; with Seaford - Delmar it makes 97.4 mi against 97.2 mi documented (Fowler SL 216 table 3, Wilmington 0.0 - Delmar 97.2). Follows OSM's New Castle Secondary and Delmarva Secondary (old_railway_operator PRR, noted PB&W (Delaware)); OpenHistoricalMap's 1852 New Castle and Wilmington and 1856 Delaware Railroad ways lie within 7 m of it except one vertex (114 m). The first ~1.5 mi from Wilmington station shares the main line to the branch junction.

segments.note: The PW&B's Delaware Division: Wilmington - New Castle - Bear over the New Castle and Wilmington (opened late 1852, PW&B; sold to the Delaware Railroad in 1891, which the PW&B itself leased) and the Delaware Railroad south to Seaford (Middletown Sept 1855, Dover Jan 1856, Seaford Dec 1856). 'The PW&B took over operations of the Delaware RR on January 1, 1857' (Wikipedia PW&B; Wikipedia Delaware Railroad: 'Starting in 1857, the PW&B operated the line as its Delaware Division'). The first Fowler letter on the Wilmington - Bear part is 1858 (n); 1857 there rests on the Delaware Railroad's through trains, which had to use it to reach Wilmington. The PRR bought a majority of PW&B stock in 1881; that is a stock purchase, not a lease, and the PW&B stayed the operating company (it leased the B&P to itself in 1891 and kept issuing its own annual reports), so 1881 is not a split here. 1902 is the end of this company: the PW&B merged with the Baltimore and Potomac into the Philadelphia, Baltimore and Washington on 1 Nov 1902; the line carried on under the PB&W (see the Pennsylvania Railroad layer). Headway is an estimate, not counted from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: 1 Jan 1857 operation from Wikipedia PW&B and Wikipedia Delaware Railroad; opening dates from Wikipedia Delaware Railroad; Fowler SL 216 table 3 n (1858). Headway not sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced except one approximated leg (a 0.1 mi straight join at Conowingo, see below): 38.99 mi drawn Port Deposit - Octoraro - Peach Bottom - Pequea - Safe Harbor - Columbia against about 39 mi documented (Fowler SL 217 table 23, 43.6 from Perryville less 4.3 mi Perryville - Port Deposit). Mostly the OSM 'Port Road Branch' (PRR, noted PB&W). LATER-ALIGNMENT CAVEAT (Rule 2): Conowingo Dam drowned the original line between Octoraro and Pilot, relocated 1927-29. Below Rowlandville to about 1 mi above Octoraro the drawing uses OpenHistoricalMap's 1877-1928 ways (spliced in), then the approximated 0.1 mi straight join to the relocated line; from there to about Pilot (roughly 2.7 mi) it draws the 1928 RELOCATED Port Road, a later alignment than this era, because the drowned grade is not mapped. Whether Holtwood (1910) or Safe Harbor (1931) dams moved the line is not established; north of Pilot the modern track is drawn.

segments.note: Columbia and Port Deposit ('Port Road'): Rowlandville - Port Deposit 1868, completed to Columbia 1877, all leased to the PW&B (Wikipedia C&PD). Completion is not proof of passenger trains: the only Fowler letter on the line is q (1884 Official Guide) at Washington Borough, so it is drawn from 1884; the bracket is 1877-1902. Trains reached Perryville over the PW&B's Port Deposit Branch, which is not drawn (no dated passenger evidence). Wikipedia's statement that the PRR controlled the PW&B in 1866 is anachronistic and is not used. 1902 is the end of this company: the PW&B merged with the Baltimore and Potomac into the Philadelphia, Baltimore and Washington on 1 Nov 1902; the line carried on under the PB&W (see the Pennsylvania Railroad layer). Headway is an estimate, not counted from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: 1884 start from Fowler SL 217 table 23 letter q (1884G) at Washington Borough; 1877 lease from Wikipedia C&PD. Headway not sourced.
